whyThisShow: This is Brent Mydland's first concert with the Grateful Dead, making it a genuine before-and-after moment in band history — one listener noted it was the "opening concert with The Good Ol' Grateful Dead" featuring Brent [source: 'Brent Mydland’s opening concert with The Good Ol’ Grateful Dead']. The band came in prepared: one attendee attributed the tightness directly to rehearsal time put in to bring Brent up to speed [source: 'They are pretty tight here. Must be from all the rehearsing they did to get Brent up to speed']. The setlist is deep and well-stocked — one fan called it "one of my favorites, just missing Terrapin and Franklins" [source: 'The set list is one of my favorites, just missing Terrapin and Franklins']. The recording is a soundboard, circulated widely enough to rack up 85 reviews on Archive, and remains unreleased officially — which only adds to the community interest in this tape.
listenFor: New Minglewood Blues is the obvious first stop: one listener described Brent raging in with his organ just as Jerry was winding up, delivering "a massive solo in minglewood, for not ever playing live with the band before" [source: 'Brent rips out a massive solo in minglewood, for not ever playing live with the band before']. Looks Like Rain carries a bit of legend from those who were there — one attendee remembered "Bobby magically making it rain on command during LLR" [source: 'Bobby magically making it rain on command during LLR']. The sound quality is described as "a little 79ish" by one listener, so go in with that expectation for the SBD [source: 'the sound quality is a little 79ish']. The second set — Estimated through Wharf Rat — is where the band's rehearsal investment tends to show itself most.
context: April 22, 1979 at Spartan Stadium in San Jose was a Bill Graham-produced outdoor event, with the Greg Kihn Band and Charlie Daniels Band on the bill before the Dead [source: 'Opening band Greg Khin Band, Charlie Daniels Band and Bill Graham Grateful Dead Event extravaganza']. It was the first show after Keith Godchaux and Donna Godchaux departed the band, with Brent Mydland stepping in on keyboards for the first time in a live setting [source: 'First concert without Keith and Donna']. The best-circulating recording is a soundboard (identifier: gd79-04-22.sbd.bennett.12001.sbeok.shnf) and the show has never received an official release.
funFact: One attendee was so far under the influence that he misremembered the setlist entirely, convinced they played Here Comes Sunshine when the sun broke through the clouds — "apparently not" [source: 'I thought they played Here Comes Sunshine when the sun broke out momentarily) but apparently not'].
headline: Brent's first night, Spartan Stadium, April '79.
